cases.title: Door scene: figure reads as floating behind a foreground table
cases.context_before_feedback: Brief: Ren (friend/neighbor character, flat soft-vector style) at the apartment door with a small box of spare light bulbs; selected presence channel was phone plus door/hallway; the packet said no new location art beyond a doorway view. The lead composed Ren in a hallway doorway seen from inside a warm interior, with a console table (key bowl, mug) in the foreground, a lamp and sofa arm at left, and the table top cropping Ren at the chest. The lead presented this as 'close framing ... the console crop acceptable, or full height' and recommended keeping the crop.
cases.what_the_image_showed_before: Lead's own description of the PNG (confidence medium; the lead viewed it in this chat): Ren centered in a doorway with a cooler hallway behind and a door across the hall; a wooden table with a mug and a small green pot spans the lower third, its top edge crossing Ren's torso and the lower part of the box; floor boards visible left and right below a wall line; faint indigo sprout marks on the neck and the forearm. The box and a bare forearm with a hand shape sit at the lower right of Ren, partly overlapped by the table.
cases.missing_context: It is not recorded whether the owner had looked at the round-2 door scene before this exchange (their earlier round-2 answers were typed through the question tool about hair, art direction and rules). No owner screenshot or annotation of the door scene exists.

The box, forearm and hand shape exist in both the before and after versions (same R-box-arm group apart from the removed tattoo stroke), so any hand/box question for a reviewer is not answered by the owner's words. Treat that region as unlabeled by the owner.

cases.title: Apartment scenes: body framing, seating and close versus wide
cases.context_before_feedback: Request: composed drawings of Ren in the player's apartment (chair, couch, standing elsewhere) and an answer whether the apartment kit's fixed one-point-perspective camera makes that easy without drawing more of Ren's body. The lead inserted a bust-only Ren into the kit's own camera at real depth so nearer furniture (redrawn sofa arms and cushions, the kitchen bar) hid the chest cut; a narrow sofa stood in for a chair because the kit has no armchair. Later the lead refreshed two scenes with newer outfits and, in the review step, asked the owner: framing 'Both, by moment (recommended)' / 'Close only' / 'Wide only'; chair 'Reuse the narrow sofa (recommended)' / 'Draw an armchair' / 'No seat'; poses; and whether to draw a floor game-night scene.
cases.what_the_image_showed_before: Lead's description (confidence medium-high; source is the lead's camera notes plus the viewed renders): in the wide couch and bar scenes Ren appears small in a full room, chest cut hidden behind furniture; in the two medium crops Ren fills more of the frame, again with the cut hidden by furniture; the narrow-sofa scene put Ren in a small sofa left of the main couch. In no scene did a visible bust cut-off line appear in open space.
cases.missing_context: What the owner actually looked at before answering is not recorded precisely: the lead opened a review page of the five refreshed scenes in the shared browser pane and described each. The owner never commented on individual scenes before stating the framing rule. Whether the owner had opened the earlier index.png is unknown.

cases.what_changed_afterward: The lead recorded close framing as the chosen look with the stated rule, treated the narrow sofa as not wanted, and drew a new close scene: couch removed (the kit's 'removed' state), Ren behind the coffee table, a flat board game with pawns on the table top (added through the spec's onTable list because items at the table's depth were hidden by the slab), no duck. The owner then asked for the duck on the blue book facing the board, and the lead set the living-room anchor to the top of the magazine stack for that scene.

classification: new requirement introduced later (close framing; body must end at the scene bottom unless an object hides it)
possible visible-defect principle stated generally (cut-off body in an uncut scene), applied to scenes that did not show it
cases.reviewer_could_know: A reviewer could reasonably check whether any figure is cut off in open space and whether furniture hides the cut. A reviewer could not know the owner's preference for close-only framing, nor that a narrow sofa would be unwanted. The older wide scenes satisfy the owner's own conditional ('unless lower body obscured by scene object'), so the rule is a stated requirement, not a defect those scenes showed.
cases.hand_box_note: Not applicable; Ren is bust-only in all scenes and no hand/box contact occurs. The board game and duck contact the table top, which the lead, not the owner, checked.
known_limitations: The scenes index.png is from the first generation; the refreshed set seen at the time of the rule has only SVG sources and one partial pane screenshot (scene 1 and the top of scene 2).
The first floor-scene render used a wrong crop that cut off Ren's head; that failed intermediate was never saved or shown.
The lead's own failed attempt (blanket prop, then removed) was not captured.
The owner may have meant 'desk' as something other than the coffee table; the lead asked and the owner answered 'coffee table'.
Rendering through headless Edge differs from any in-game camera; not checked in a game layout.

cases.title: Accepted control (tool apron) beside an unexplained 'not yet' (puffer vest) in one message
cases.context_before_feedback: The owner asked for two more outfits from the earlier outfit sheets: a tool apron over a tee and a puffer vest (message 2026-11-01T00:50:20Z, 'tool apron over tee, puffer vest'). Two Haiku helpers drew them from the Gemini outfit sheet cells (apron: workwear sheet bottom-left; vest: weather sheet top-right) using a shared brief; the lead viewed both renders, judged the apron fine, found the vest's quilting read like scales with a tall boxy collar, and redrew it as v2 (straight seam lines, shorter collar) before showing the sheet. The Gemini cell shows an open puffy vest; the lead's v2 was a closed vest.
cases.what_the_image_showed_before: Lead's description of renders (confidence high; viewed): apron - grey-blue short-sleeve tee, brown apron with neck straps, one pocket with two tool handles, waist strap, bare upper arms with the arm tattoo on the viewer's right. Vest v2 - olive closed vest with three curved horizontal seam lines, gold zipper pull, short stand collar over cream sleeves; flat rather than puffy.
cases.missing_context: The owner gave no reason for 'does not yet'. Whether the owner saw v1 is unlikely (it was not on the sheet). The owner's reference expectation for a puffer vest is unknown.
